packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files. Beyond the brief: (a) a directory listing of the packet showed the filename packet.json; I did not open it. (b) To read the tiles closely I cut each native tile (002, 003, 005, 006, 008, 009, 011, 012, 014, 015, 017, 018, 020, 021, 023, 024) into four overlapping quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, ~100-150 px overlap) in my scratchpad and viewed those. (c) The viewer dropped several images from my context before I could use them: the overview images 001, 004, 007, 010, 013, 016, 019, 022, the first view of tile 005, and most of tile 003. I re-viewed the 002 quadrants and the bottom-left quadrant of 003. I could not re-view all of 005 and 003, so face 1 (tiles 002/003) and face 2 top (005) are read only in part. See LIMITATIONS.

Line numbering: lines are counted from the first text line visible in each native tile. In the quadrant crops, the top half covers roughly lines 1-10 and the bottom half roughly lines 9-19. Lines in the overlap band are read once only. Numbers are approximate to within about one line.

=====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations only)
=====================================================================
- Eight faces, seemingly each covered by a pair of native tiles (upper and lower). All are fragments of one written column, perhaps cut from a binding: there are holes, a tear and patching (black cloth backing shows through the losses). Single column per fragment. In each case the left or right edge of the column is lost or cropped, so lines are truncated on one side.
- Script: small Gothic textualis with heavy abbreviation. Ink is brown, faded in places. Faces 5 and 6 (tiles 014/015, 017/018) show strong offset/show-through ghost text and are hard to read.
- Rubrication: red-stroked capitals and paraphs on faces 7 and 8 (tiles 021, 023). In 021 there is a red bracket/frame at the left margin enclosing several lines (column of red horizontal strokes), and red-touched capitals "C" at lines 6 and 8 of 021-b and a red C at 021-d line 7. In 023 there is a red-touched capital "C"/"T" mid-line (line 3) and a red stroke in line 5. In 024-d, faint red ruling/frame lines appear at the right edge.
- Marginalia: tile 011 left margin has later or contemporary small-hand notes: "[?]receptor" (or "deceptor"?) and "R(ebecca)? rebecca. iacob / [illegible] esau(?)". Tile 018 left margin: "R(?). sepl(chr)um? / s(ecun)d(um)? ..." (looks like "R. sepl[...]" / "sb incom[...]" / "ex"); seemingly a note repeating a word from the text ("seplchrum" in the same line).
- Interlinear superscript corrections/additions appear in several places (e.g. 006 "ar" over "carnal", 011 "ar" over "ardore", 017 "s(?)" above lines).
- Biblical-citation-like references appear inline with abbreviated book names and chapter numerals (e.g. "luc.", "mach.", "ez.", "gen.", "ps.", "Io."), set off by points. Tentative interpretation: continuous prose (sermon or treatise style) with scriptural citations and Old Testament exempla, not a glossed text. No running titles visible. A stamp impression (a rectangular library-style stamp with lettering, not legible) appears on 014/017 (top) and on 023 (right).

=====================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED
=====================================================================
I read the clearest connected prose from each face, giving priority to lines with citations (book + chapter) and named persons, since those make a later source match checkable. Unread or weakly read: most of face 1 (002/003); the right half of face 2 upper (005); much of faces 5 and 6, where show-through is heavy; and the lowest lines of several tiles. A wider view or re-shot of 002/003/005 without show-through would help. Note that the right half of each face is cut off at the column edge (or is the margin) in most tiles, so line ends are truncated.

Conventions: (expansion) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain; [illegible] = unreadable; [hole] = physical loss; | = line truncated at crop/edge.

=====================================================================
3. TRANSCRIPTION
=====================================================================
